# `chat.*` — messages

Mix of officially documented methods (improved here with observed quirks) and
one undocumented method (`chat.command`).

## `chat.scheduleMessage` (documented)

- **Docs:** https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.scheduleMessage
- **Observed quirk not obvious from the docs:** on this workspace (Hack Club,
  Enterprise Grid), calling this with a session token — **either** the team xoxc
  or the enterprise xoxc, on **either** `slack.com` or `hackclub.slack.com` —
  always returns `{"ok": false, "error": "not_allowed_token_type"}`. This is a
  hard token-class gate, not a scope/permission issue: no xoxc/xoxd combination
  gets through it. The web client itself does not use this method for its
  "Schedule for later" UI — it uses the undocumented `drafts.create` instead
  (see `drafts.md`). If you have a real xoxb/xoxp app token with
  `chat:write` scope, that's the supported path for this method; we did not
  test that here (out of scope — this project only had session tokens for chat
  scheduling work).
- **Live-verified this session:** the `not_allowed_token_type` rejection, both
  token scopes, both hosts. Not verified: successful use with xoxb/xoxp (no
  such call was made against this method).

## `chat.scheduledMessages.list` (documented)

- **Docs:** https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.scheduledMessages.list
- **Same quirk:** `not_allowed_token_type` for both xoxc token scopes, both
  hosts. Use `drafts.list` (enterprise xoxc only) instead to see what the web
  client itself considers "scheduled" on this workspace.

## `chat.command`

- **Status:** UNDOCUMENTED.
- **Purpose (inferred from name + source):** runs a slash command server-side,
  as if it had been typed into the message composer and submitted — i.e. the
  server-side counterpart to typing `/remind ...` and hitting enter, rather than
  the outbound webhook mechanism apps register for (`commands.list` /
  `POST /interactive-endpoint`-style command dispatch is documented; this is the
  reverse, client-invoking direction).
- **Existence:** confirmed via oracle (`invalid_auth` for a garbage token, not
  `unknown_method`).
- **Live-tested:** **no.** Running an arbitrary slash command is inherently
  state-changing (many slash commands post messages, some do much more) — this
  is explicitly excluded from live-testing under the hard safety rules. Do not
  call this against real tokens without first confirming exactly which command
  string you're passing and that its effect is something you want.
- **Token type:** unknown/not tested.
- **Provenance:** `slack-ruby/slack-api-ref`,
  `methods/_undocumented/chat/chat.command.json`.
- **Params (cross-referenced from `ErikKalkoken/slackApiDoc`, not independently
  verified here):** `token` (required — their notes say the `post` scope isn't
  available through normal OAuth app config, so a legacy token is needed),
  `channel` (required, public channel ID to run the command in), `command`
  (required, e.g. `/who`, leading slash required), `text` (optional, args to
  the command). Response: `{"ok": true, "response": "..."}` for commands that
  answer inline (e.g. `/who`); most slash commands instead just post their
  output into the channel and `response` is absent.

## `chat.postMessage` with Block Kit: review-card gotchas (documented method)

- **Docs:** https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.postMessage
- **What it's from:** the HMojis submission review cards, which a bot posts
  into a review channel with approve and decline buttons. Observed on the
  Hack Club workspace on 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24.
- **`action_id` must be unique within a message.** Four buttons sharing one
  `action_id` (with the verb carried in `value`) make Slack reject the
  entire message. Give each button its own id, for example
  `hm_review:yes` and `hm_review:no`.
- **Image blocks only render PNG, JPEG and GIF.** For other types (WebP was
  the case hit), post a section with a link instead, or convert the image
  first.
- **Linking an image you also show makes Slack show it twice.** The card's
  text linked the same URL the image block used, and Slack unfurled that
  link as a second copy. Two fixes, both now used:
  - keep the URL out of the text
  - pass `unfurl_links=false` and `unfurl_media=false`
- **Image URLs are fetched with no auth headers.** An `image_url` has to be
  reachable without an `Authorization` header, so a private image needs a
  capability in the URL instead: a random, per-image `?cap=` value written
  only into the card and checked by the server.
- **Posting to a user id as the bot.** `chat.postMessage` with
  `channel=U…` (bot token, `chat:write`) delivers to the bot's DM with that
  user, with no `conversations.open` step needed.

## `chat.postMessage` as an RSS-style bot: identity, newer blocks, threads (documented method)

Observed 2026-10-28 on the Hack Club workspace with a bot `xoxb` that has
`chat:write`, `chat:write.customize` and `files:write`. Everything below was
called for real unless marked otherwise.

- **Custom name and icon.** `username` and `icon_url` were accepted on the
  same call as `blocks`, and again on a **thread reply** (`thread_ts` set), so a
  reply can look like it came from the same persona. We did not test a bot
  without `chat:write.customize`, so what happens without it is unconfirmed.
- **Newer blocks post fine as a bot.** A message with a `section` (button
  `accessory`) and a `context` block, then a thread reply with a
  `data_visualization` block (a `bar` chart with a negative series, and a
  `line` chart), a `table` block and a `section`, all returned `ok:true`.
  `conversations.replies` then listed the reply's blocks as
  `['data_visualization', 'table', 'section']`. We did not check how they
  render. Per the docs a message may hold at most 2 `data_visualization`
  blocks, and `alert` blocks are modal-only (docs, not tested).
- **`table` + `column_settings`.** The docs say to use `null` for a column
  that should keep the defaults. `blocks.validate` rejects that:
  `invalid_blocks`, `{"code":"invalid_type","message":"must provide an object","pointer":"/1/column_settings/0"}`.
  An explicit object per column (`{"align": "left"}`, `{"align": "right"}`)
  passed. A table cell used here was `{"type":"raw_text","text":"…"}`.
- **Top-level `text` is still the notification fallback** when `blocks` are
  present; send a short plain summary there.
- **Escape feed text.** `&`, `<` and `>` in text you did not write must be
  escaped (`&amp;`, `&lt;`, `&gt;`) or `<!channel>` / `<@U…>` in it will
  notify people.
- **Attachments with mrkdwn.** For legacy `attachments`, `text` is only parsed
  as mrkdwn if the attachment lists it in `mrkdwn_in` (`["text"]`); the
  `<url|label>` link syntax, `*bold*` and bullets then render.

### `blocks.validate` (documented method)

- **It needs no token.** Called with no `Authorization` header, it returned
  `{"ok": true}` for valid blocks and the `invalid_blocks` shape above for
  invalid ones (live, 2026-10-28). It also works with a bot token.
- **Error shape.** `{"ok":false,"error":"invalid_blocks","errors":[{"code":…,"message":…,"pointer":"/1/column_settings/0"}]}`
  — `pointer` is a JSON pointer into the `blocks` array you sent.
- **Passes:** `section` with a `button` accessory, `context` with `mrkdwn`,
  `table`, and `data_visualization` (`bar` and `line`) validated `ok:true`.
- **Pass the array as `blocks=<json>`** (form-encoded). A whole message works
  as `message=`, a modal/home view as `view=`, per the docs.

### What Slack's own RSS app posts (source: a message event the site owner pasted, not an API call)

- `subtype: "bot_message"` with the feed item title as `text`, the feed's name
  as `username` (for example `xkcd.com`), `bot_id`, and an `edited` object stamped
  about 2 seconds after `ts` (presumably Slack adding the unfurl; not confirmed).
- `icons.image_36`, `image_48`, `image_72`: `https://a.slack-edge.com/…/img/services/rss_<size>.png`.
- One `attachments` entry per item: `title`, `title_link`, `from_url`,
  `original_url`, `fallback` (`"<feed>: <title>"`), `author_name`/`author_link`
  (the feed's site), `service_icon`, `text` (here the xkcd alt text),
  `image_url` with `image_width`/`image_height`/`image_bytes`, and
  `media_type: "external_link"`. The `blocks` are a single `rich_text` link to
  the item. That is the shape to copy for an RSS-like bot.
- **Where the native bot's fields come from** (inferred by putting a native post next to the item's feed XML on 2026-10-28; not tested by
  subscribing a feed): xkcd's item `description` is only
  `<img src="…" title="…" alt="…">`, and the native post's `image_url` is that `src` while its `text` is
  `[Title text] "<the img title>"`. So the bot reads the first `<img>` for the image and an image's `title` attribute for the text. For a feed
  whose `description` is a whole HTML document (sdmp.izie.top before 2026-10-28), the post's text was the tags stripped with nothing
  between list items (`…(6)+ ai.alpha.…`), so a plain-text `description` with its own separators reads far better, with the full markup
  in `content:encoded` for readers.
- **Legacy attachment fields accepted by `chat.postMessage`** (xoxb, live 2026-10-28, `ok:true`; rendering not inspected): `footer`,
  `footer_icon` (we passed a site's `.ico` favicon, which may not render, since the docs list image types), `ts` (shown beside the
  footer), `author_name`/`author_link`, `color`, `title_link`, `from_url`, `image_url`, and `mrkdwn_in: ["text"]`.
- **Slack's RSS app, per its help page** (docs, not tested by us; <https://slack.com/help/articles/218688467>): `/feed subscribe <address>`,
  `/feed list` (shows each feed's unique ID number), `/feed remove <ID>`, `/feed help`; feeds can also be managed across channels from the
  app's page in the Marketplace. It keeps a bookmark with the date of the last item and only posts items dated later, so an item that
  arrives with an older date is never posted. Everyone except guests can use it. RSS and Atom only.
- **Guests in the API** (docs): `users.info` returns `is_restricted` (multi-channel guest) and `is_ultra_restricted` (single-channel guest) on the
  `user` object; either being true is how you recognise a guest. We use that to keep guests out of a feed command.
- **`footer` text is linkified.** A bare domain sent as `footer` (`xkcd.com`) came back from `conversations.history` as
  `<http://xkcd.com|xkcd.com>` (live, 2026-10-28), so Slack auto-links it. Sent `ts` came back unchanged as the attachment's `ts`.
- **`conversations.history` shows custom-identity posts with a `username`** (the persona name) alongside the bot's `bot_id`; the text and
  attachments are returned as sent.
- **`blocks` and `attachments` in one `chat.postMessage`** (xoxb, live 2026-10-28): both are accepted, and `blocks` render above the
  attachment card. Passing `blocks` means Slack no longer adds its own `rich_text` block for `text`; `text` is then only the notification
  fallback. A `section` with a `button` accessory that has a `url` and an `action_id` passed `blocks.validate` and posted. Use it to
  keep a call to action (a podcast's Listen button) from being cut off under a long attachment `text`.
- **Where a button ends up** (observed 2026-10-28 in the site owner's client): a `section` block's `accessory` button is drawn on the **right** of
  its text, and blocks are drawn **above** a message's `attachments`, so a button put in `blocks` next to an attachment card sits at the
  very top of the message. Buttons in an `actions` block are drawn at the **left**, under the content above them. To get a card with the
  button at the bottom left, build the whole card from blocks and drop the attachment.
- **The `container` block works in a bot message** (xoxb, live 2026-10-28; `blocks.validate` `ok:true`, `chat.postMessage` ok, and
  `conversations.history` returns it as `blocks[0].type == "container"`): `title` (plain_text, 150), `subtitle` (we sent `mrkdwn`, including a
  `<!date^…|fallback>` token), `width: "wide"`, an `icon` image, and `child_blocks` of `section`, `image`, `context` and `actions` were all
  accepted. This is the block `ingoau/huddlefm` builds its player message from (`src/coordinator.ts`). Card and carousel are covered in the next bullet. An icon URL ending in `.ico` is a poor bet; stick to png/jpg/gif.
- **`carousel` and `card` blocks in a bot message** (xoxb, live 2026-10-28; `blocks.validate` `ok:true`, `chat.postMessage` ok): a `carousel`
  takes 1 to 10 `card` blocks. A `card` accepted a `plain_text` `title`, a `mrkdwn` `subtitle` (with a `<!date^…|…>` token), a `hero_image`
  (`image` element), a `mrkdwn` `body` (docs: 200 chars) and `actions` buttons (docs: up to 3). Button `action_id`s must be unique across the
  whole message, so number them per card. We use one carousel when a feed has several new items at once.
- **`data_table` block in a message** (docs read 2026-10-28, a message with it validated and posted; the same limits as `table` but richer): the
  first row is the header, every row needs the same number of cells, header cells need non-empty text (an empty header cell is rejected with
  `must be more than 0 characters`), `caption` is required, `page_size` 1-100, up to 200 body rows and 20 columns. A cell can be `raw_text`,
  `raw_number`, `rich_text` (not in the header) or an `action_cell` holding a `button` with an optional `fallback` cell for clients without
  action cells. Per the docs the buttons are disabled in a shared or copied message, and a `data_table` can't sit inside a `container`.
- **`data_table` with button cells, as built and validated by us** (live 2026-10-28, `blocks.validate` `ok:true` for the channel-scoped and the
  all-channels versions, and a message with one posted ok): header cells as `raw_text`; a number column as `raw_number` with `value` and `text`;
  a link as a `rich_text` cell containing a `link` element; a channel as a `rich_text` cell containing a `channel` element
  (`{"type":"channel","channel_id":"C…"}`); and a button as an `action_cell` with `element` (a `button` with `action_id` and `value`) and a
  `fallback` `raw_text` cell. We put the row's id in the button `value` and its verb in the `action_id`
  (`feed_pause_3`), then answer the click with one `app.action` regex handler. A click arrives as a normal `block_actions` payload.
- **Mobile.** Slack's blog post on the new blocks (slack.dev/build-richer-agent-experiences-with-block-kit) says they render natively on web,
  desktop, iOS and Android and lists Card, Alert and Carousel as available and Data Table as "coming soon"; neither it nor the block docs
  give a per-client matrix or say what an unsupported client shows. We have not tested a phone. Always send a useful top-level `text`.
- **Link buttons still send a click to the app.** A button with `url` opens the link in the client, but Slack also delivers a
  `block_actions` payload for it, so the app should acknowledge it. Give the button a fixed `action_id` and register one no-op handler; with a
  Bolt app and no handler the click is "unhandled" (the app returns a 404). We did not test how the client shows an unacknowledged click.
- **Reading custom-identity posts back.** `conversations.history` returned each message's own `username` correctly with both a bot and a
  user token (live, 2026-10-28). A reader that labels messages by `bot_id` can show them all under one name: the Slack MCP channel reader we
  tried named every message from our bot after the oldest custom `username` in the page it read (6 messages -> the first name; the newest 3 ->
  the oldest of those 3). The site owner's own Slack client showed the correct names, so this is the reader, not what Slack stores. Don't
  trust a bot_id-keyed name when checking what a persona posted; read `username` per message.
- **A pasted bare domain** (`blog.izie.top/feed.xml`) arrives with `text` as the
  bare text and a `rich_text` `link` element whose `url` is the full
  `https://…` and `truncated: true` (message event, pasted by the site owner).

# `client.*` — internal web-client boot/sync endpoints

**UNDOCUMENTED.** Not in `docs.slack.dev`/`api.slack.com/methods`. These are the
internal endpoints the Slack web/desktop client itself calls on load and while
running, found via `korotovsky/slack-mcp-server`'s Edge-API notes and a public
Enterprise Grid network-traffic reverse-engineering writeup, then confirmed to
exist via the existence oracle and partly live-tested read-only.

All calls are the usual `POST https://slack.com/api/client.<name>`,
form-encoded, `Authorization: Bearer <xoxc>` + `Cookie: d=<xoxd>` — same
dispatcher as documented methods, not the separate Edge-API cache host (see
`edge-api.md` for that one).

## `client.boot`

- **Status:** undocumented. **Live-verified.**
- **Purpose:** boots a single **team's** web-client state (as opposed to the
  org-wide `client.userBoot`).
- **Token:** team-scoped xoxc/xoxd. Enterprise-scoped xoxc gets
  `enterprise_is_restricted` — this method is explicitly team-level, not org-level.
- **Params tried:** none (empty POST body).
- **Response:** `{"ok": true, ...}` with team xoxc (full payload not captured/kept —
  only top-level shape checked to avoid retaining workspace data). With enterprise
  xoxc: `{"ok": false, "error": "enterprise_is_restricted"}`.
- **Gotcha:** this is the mirror-image failure mode of `client.userBoot` below —
  the two are scoped to opposite token classes. If you're writing a "boot the
  client" helper, you need both tokens and to try one then the other.
- **Provenance:** name from reverse-engineering gist (sshh12) "boot" call list;
  scoping behavior discovered live this session.

## `client.userBoot`

- **Status:** undocumented. **Live-verified.**
- **Purpose:** boots the **org-wide** user/client state across the whole
  Enterprise Grid organization — channels, DMs, prefs, starred items, subteams,
  workspaces list, etc. This is the "give me everything about this user across
  the whole Grid org" bootstrap call.
- **Token:** enterprise-scoped xoxc/xoxd required. Team-scoped xoxc gets
  `internal_error` (not `team_is_restricted` as with most other org-wide
  methods here — worth noting as an inconsistency in Slack's own error handling).
- **Params tried:** none.
- **Response (top-level keys only, redacted):** `ok, self, team, workspaces,
  channels, channels_priority, ims, non_threadable_channels,
  thread_only_channels, read_only_channels, temporary_channel_expirations,
  starred, subteams, prefs, prefs_version, dnd, links, account_types,
  can_access_client_v2, has_more_mpdms, is_open, is_europe,
  is_content_reporting_enabled, is_eligible_invited_user_glow_up,
  is_slack_first_crm, mobile_app_requires_upgrade, accept_tos_url,
  app_commands_cache_ts, cache_ts_version, cache_version, emoji_cache_ts,
  translations_cache_ts, paid_features, default_workspace, slack_route`.
  (Actual values — channel IDs, team name, self user object, etc. — deliberately
  not retained/quoted; this is genuinely the full state the web client bootstraps
  with, so treat it as sensitive/PII-bearing and don't dump it verbatim to a file.)
- **Gotcha:** heavy payload — this is effectively "give me your whole account,"
  call sparingly and never persist the raw response outside memory.
- **Provenance:** name + purpose from korotovsky/slack-mcp-server Edge-API docs
  ("fetches workspace bootstrap information... enterprise Grid only"); response
  shape confirmed live this session.

## `client.counts`

- **Status:** undocumented. **Live-verified** (existence + scoping only; did not
  retain response content).
- **Purpose:** unread/mention/badge counts across channels and DMs — what powers
  the little unread-count badges in the sidebar. Referenced as the "efficient"
  unread-detection path (vs. calling `conversations.info` once per channel with
  xoxp) by korotovsky/slack-mcp-server.
- **Token:** enterprise xoxc/xoxd. Team xoxc -> `team_is_restricted`.
- **Params tried:** none; real client calls likely pass a `thread_counts`/channel
  filter — not explored further to avoid over-probing.
- **Provenance:** korotovsky/slack-mcp-server ("efficient unread message
  detection... requires xoxc+xoxd session tokens").

## `client.extras`

- **Status:** undocumented. **Partially live-verified** (exists; not fully
  exercised).
- **Purpose:** unclear from name alone — likely auxiliary boot data not included
  in the main `userBoot`/`boot` payload (secondary workspaces, extra metadata).
- **Token:** enterprise xoxc/xoxd (team xoxc -> `team_is_restricted`).
- **Response with no params (enterprise xoxc):** `{"ok": false, "error":
  "invalid_arguments"}` — needs at least one param we didn't supply. Not probed
  further (unclear what's safe to pass without knowing the shape; left as a
  documented gap).
- **Provenance:** name from the Enterprise Grid reverse-engineering gist's boot
  call list.

## `client.shouldReload`

- **Status:** undocumented. **Partially live-verified.**
- **Purpose:** tells the client whether its cached JS build is stale and it
  should force-reload — part of Slack's incremental-boot/version-check flow.
- **Token:** enterprise xoxc/xoxd (team xoxc -> `team_is_restricted`).
- **Response with no params (enterprise xoxc):** `{"ok": false, "error":
  "bad_build_version_ts"}` — wants a build/version timestamp param.
- **Provenance:** name from the reverse-engineering gist's boot call list;
  matches Slack's public engineering blog post on "incremental boot"
  (`slack.engineering/getting-to-slack-faster-with-incremental-boot`), which
  describes the *concept* (not the private API) of build-version reload checks.

## `client.dms`

- **Status:** undocumented. **Existence confirmed via oracle; not live-called
  with real tokens** (no read-only call attempted — didn't want to guess at
  required filter params for a DM-history endpoint without knowing its shape).
- **Purpose:** per korotovsky/slack-mcp-server docs, "direct message history
  filters" — likely a DM-scoped listing/sync call, part of the same Edge-routing
  family as `client.counts`.
- **Token:** session tokens; Enterprise Grid, per the same source.
- **Provenance:** korotovsky/slack-mcp-server Edge-API documentation (via
  DeepWiki summary of that repo); existence confirmed directly this session
  (`client.dms` + garbage token -> `invalid_auth`, not `unknown_method`).

"Observed argument names" are names passed at call sites in the client's code: real, but partial, and not a schema (see `datamine-2026-10.md`). Required/optional is unknown. camelCase names may be snake_case on the wire.

## What the pieces do (inferred)

- **Create / join:** `createAndStart` creates a channel and starts its agent session; `create` and `join` are the client-side variants ("join from an origin the user can see" is a client string); `listSupportedApps` lists which apps/agents can back one.
- **Views:** `getView` / `getBlockKitView` render the channel surface.
- **Pull requests:** `getPullRequestConnection`, `getPrWorkObject`, `getSummary`, `getDiff`, `getMergeStatus`, `requestReviewers`, `addReviewComment`, `submitReview` and `mergePullRequest` cover the PR lifecycle inside the channel. Their observed arguments (`prUrl`, `headSha`, `channelId`, `revision`, `event`, `text`) fit that.
- **`action`:** a generic action endpoint for the channel (older builds).

## Related client strings

- Naming: "Code channel", "Code channels", "Public code channel", "Code Channel Command".
- Lifecycle: "Create a code channel", "New code channel", "Search code channels", "No code channels yet", "Auto-close stale code channels", "When a code channel is archived", "Close an MPIM, IM, or code channel".
- Pull requests: "PR status", "PR approved / closed / merged / feedback", "Create PR", "Filter pull requests".

- Adjacent: "Agent sessions" strings suggest code channels are backed by agent sessions.

# `conversations.*` — conversations

Documented `conversations.*` methods (`list`, `info`, `history`, `members`,
`replies`, `open`, etc.) are unchanged from official docs, with one gotcha
worth recording:

- `conversations.open` with `users=U...` returns a `D...` channel id for the
  1:1 DM — used throughout this project to resolve a user id into something
  `drafts.create`'s `destinations` param will accept (which rejects raw `U...`
  ids with `invalid_channel`).

### Proving who posted a message (a bot reading its own DMs)

These are documented behaviours, but the combination is easy to get wrong. The
HMojis server uses it to verify a Slack account: the user's own client posts a
one-time code in a DM with a bot, and the server reads it back with the bot's
token.

- **Author.** `conversations.history` on an IM the bot is part of returns
  each message's author in the message's own `user` field. That is Slack's
  attestation, not something the poster can forge.
- **Bot scopes.** The bot needs `im:history` and `im:read`.
- **Ruling out the bot's own posts.** Messages the bot posted carry
  `bot_id`, `subtype: "bot_message"`, or both.
- **Who the DM is with.** `conversations.info` on the IM (as the bot) returns
  `is_im: true` and `user` set to the other party. Cross-check that against
  the author.
- **Other people's DMs are invisible.** A DM between two other users isn't
  readable by the bot: `conversations.info` and `conversations.history`
  return `channel_not_found`. A client can't point the reader at a DM it
  doesn't share with the bot.
- **Users DMing the bot.** For the user to message the bot at all, the app's
  App Home needs `messages_tab_enabled: true` and
  `messages_tab_read_only_enabled: false`.
- **Verified:** relied on by the HMojis verifier in production since
  2026-09-24, and covered by tests against a Slack mock. Not independently
  probed by this project's `probe.py`.

This file also covers three undocumented additions.

## Leaving a channel (live-tested 2026-09-28)

All of this was exercised with ordinary **browser-session accounts** (xoxc + `d=`
cookie, no admin/manager rights, no app) driving `conversations.leave` across 51
separate accounts on this workspace, plus the undocumented
`conversations.bulkLeave`. Method: leave a public channel the accounts were
members of, then re-read membership with `users.conversations` and
`conversations.info` to confirm.

### `conversations.leave` — live-verified

Previously `docs-only`. Now confirmed end-to-end: **51 of 51 accounts left a
public channel they were in, 0 failures**, each with its own token.

- **Self-leave needs no special rights.** No `channels:manage`, no
  channel-manager, no admin. This is the practical difference from
  `conversations.kick` below, and it's why "get a bot out of a channel it was
  temporarily invited to" doesn't need an inviter account at all.
- **`cant_leave_general`** on this workspace's one `is_general: true` channel
  (`C0266FRGT`), for every account and on both hosts. This is a hard server-side
  rule, not a permissions problem.
- **`not_in_channel`** when the account was never a member — the normal result
  for a bulk sweep across accounts that weren't all in the target.
- **`channel_not_found`** for a *private* channel the caller isn't in. A private
  channel is invisible to non-members, so a self-leave is impossible precisely
  when someone might most want it; the account can only be removed by somebody
  who can already see the channel.
- **`invalid_arguments`** if you pass a channel *name* (`announcements`) instead
  of an id. Ids only.

### `conversations.bulkLeave` — UNDOCUMENTED, live-verified, and a trap

`params` here were previously "generated TS types, cross-referenced not
independently verified" and `verified` was `existence-only`. Both are now
settled by live calls.

- **Status:** UNDOCUMENTED (`3kh0/slack-datamine` build 132396).
- **Purpose:** the client's bulk "leave channels" flow. Leaves the calling
  account from the conversation(s) named in `channels`.
- **`channels` takes a plain channel id string** — `channels=C…`. Verified: this
  form actually left `#lounge` (membership dropped on re-read; rejoined
  afterwards to restore the original state).
- **A JSON-array encoding silently does nothing.** `channels=["C…"]` returns
  `ok: true` and the account is *still* a member. Since the generated type only
  said "string", the obvious "it's a list, so send a list" reading is a silent
  no-op — worth knowing before trusting a bulk call's success.
- **It lies about #general.** On `C0266FRGT` it returned `ok: true` with **no
  effect**: confirmed by four `users.conversations` reads over ~8s and by
  `conversations.info` still reporting `is_member: true`, while
  `conversations.leave` on the same target errors `cant_leave_general`. So the
  #general block is enforced on both code paths — `bulkLeave` just fails
  quietly instead of loudly. **Do not use `bulkLeave`'s `ok` as evidence a leave
  happened**; re-read membership instead.
- **Tokens:** works with the **enterprise** xoxc on both `hackclub.slack.com`
  and `hackclub.enterprise.slack.com`; the **team** xoxc returns
  `team_is_restricted`. (Fits the team-vs-org split in `../auth-and-tokens.md`.)
- **Not established:** the multi-id form (whether `channels` accepts a
  comma-separated list) was never tested — only the single-id case. A repeated
  `channels` param returned `channel_not_found`, but that call was confounded
  (the account had already left by then, and that error is what a not-a-member
  leave returns), so it proves nothing either way.

### `conversations.kick` — live-verified negative

Kicking **yourself** (`channel` + your own `user` id) returns
**`restricted_action`** on a non-admin account. There is no self-kick shortcut
around `conversations.leave`, and no admin token was available in this pass
(`not_an_admin`/`restricted_action` across the board, see
`methods/admin-write-scope-2026-09.md`). Use self-leave.

## `conversations.view`

- **Status:** UNDOCUMENTED.
- **Purpose (inferred from name):** likely marks a conversation as
  "viewed"/opened in the client — analogous to (but possibly distinct from) the
  documented `conversations.mark` read-cursor call.
- **Existence:** confirmed via oracle.
- **Live-tested:** **deliberately no.** Its name strongly suggests a
  view/read-state side effect (marking something read/opened is exactly the
  kind of thing the safety rules call out — "never mark anything read"), so
  even though it might resolve to a GET-shaped info call, we couldn't rule that
  out from the name alone and skipped it.
- **Provenance:** reverse-engineering gist, "Conversations & Channels" section.

## `conversations.listPrefs`

- **Status:** UNDOCUMENTED.
- **Purpose (inferred):** list per-conversation client preferences (mute state,
  notification overrides, etc.) — plural/list counterpart to a per-conversation
  prefs object.
- **Existence:** confirmed via oracle.
- **Live-tested:** no (time/scope — plausibly read-only but not confirmed).
- **Provenance:** reverse-engineering gist.

## `conversations.bulkReacjiTriggers`

- **Status:** UNDOCUMENTED.
- **Purpose (inferred):** bulk-fetch of "reacji" (automatic emoji-reaction)
  trigger configuration across conversations — config for the feature where
  certain message patterns auto-react.
- **Existence:** confirmed via oracle.
- **Live-tested:** no.
- **Provenance:** reverse-engineering gist.

# `slack-datamine` build-132396 mining -- new undocumented methods (this pass)

# Our own miner (`slack-datamine-plus`), "not in the current client", and observed params -- 2026-10-20

## Sources

- **`IzieStratt/slack-datamine-plus`** (this project's own miner, AGPL-3.0, runs from GitHub Actions every ~40 minutes): downloads the ~1,800 public JavaScript chunks of Slack's web client for the logged-in throwaway account's build, extracts API method names and the argument names used at call sites. It is listed in each entry's `source` as `IzieStratt/slack-datamine-plus (own miner)`; 1537 entries carry it.
- **`3kh0/slack-datamine`** (full git history, 2026-06-02 -> 2026-10-19): the earlier source for most undocumented names. Its recent builds only list ~250 methods because its chunk discovery broke around 2026-07-24 (see below); that is why this project built its own miner.

## "Not in the current client" (was called "removed")

`methods.json` field `not_in_client: true` means: the method name was seen in an earlier client build but is **missing from the most recent builds**. It does **not** mean Slack deleted the endpoint. The client may have stopped using it, moved it behind a flag or an A/B test, or loads it lazily in a chunk the miner did not reach. Many such methods may still answer.

- A method only gets the flag after it has been missing from **3 consecutive mined builds**, so one odd build does not flip it. It loses the flag as soon as it is seen again.
- A method the client still *mentions* (for example in log text such as "failed to call search.team") counts as present.
- Right now **412** of 2282 methods carry the flag. Documented (official) methods never do.
- The explorer hides them by default. Tick **Show methods not in the current client** to see them; they carry a grey "not in client" tag. They are also in `api/index.json` / `api/methods.txt` (`not_in_client`) and marked in the master index.

The old field names `removed` / `removed_note` no longer exist.

## Observed request parameters (`params_observed`)

Slack's client declares its API calls as "fetchers", for example `(0,S.r)("slackbotProjectsCreateFetcher","slackbot.projects.create")`, and passes the arguments where the fetcher is called. The miner collects those argument names per method.

- **623** undocumented methods now have `params_observed` (name, a type hint if the value is a literal, and how many call sites pass it). Example: `client.codeChannels.mergePullRequest` -> `channelId`, `headSha`, `prUrl`, `reason`.
- It is **not a schema**: it is stored separately and `params_known` stays `false`. The names are real (taken from Slack's own code) but the set is partial (spread arguments and values built elsewhere are invisible), nothing says which are required, types are mostly unknown, and camelCase names in the client may be snake_case on the wire. The explorer shows these as "observed (N)".
- Methods the client calls through another mechanism, or from a chunk where the fetcher is imported under a different name, have none yet.

## Why the 3kh0 miner lost most methods (checked 2026-10-19)

- Slack's client shell no longer lists the async chunks in its HTML. The chunk list lives in the public `webpack.manifest` script as a name->hash map (`__webpack_require__.u`), about 1,800 entries, and the old discovery pattern did not match that format. The collapse is visible in her history: 1,526 chunks (until 2026-07-24) -> 14.
- The 12 "failed" names (`gantry-v2.<hash>.min.js`) return `403 AccessDenied` even for old builds that mined fine, so they were never fetchable and are probably not real files.
- The real chunks are **brotli-compressed** (the `-br` in the CDN path).

| window | method names per 3kh0 build |
|---|---|
| 2026-06 -> 2026-07-14 | ~1,650 -> 1,760 |
| 2026-07-24 -> 2026-10-01 | ~450 -> 475 |
| 2026-10-15 -> now | 250 |

The miner here reads the manifest instead, which yields ~600 names from ~1,800 chunks. The older, larger counts included names that are no longer in the client.

## Code channels

See `code-channels.md`.

# `drafts.*` — scheduled/unsent message drafts

**UNDOCUMENTED.** Not in the official method list. This is the Slack web
client's actual mechanism for "schedule a message" and "save as draft" — it
supersedes the older, still-technically-documented `chat.scheduleMessage` for
session-token users on this workspace (see `chat.md` for why that path is
blocked here).

All four confirmed to exist via the oracle. `create`/`list`/`delete` were
exercised live this session (list read-only; create+delete only inside the
self-DM sandbox, immediately cleaned up). `update` was confirmed to exist but
never called for real (editing a draft is a mutation with no clear read-only
subset, so it's out of scope for live-testing per the safety rules — documented
from the same field names `create`/`delete` use).

## `drafts.create`

- **Status:** undocumented. **Live-verified** (sandbox: self-DM `D09KUP5M2N7`,
  ≥30 days out, cleaned up after).
- **Token:** works with **either** the team xoxc or the enterprise xoxc (the one
  exception among the `drafts.*` family — see `auth-and-tokens.md`).
- **Endpoint:** `POST https://slack.com/api/drafts.create`, form-encoded.
- **Params:**
  - `blocks` (string, **JSON-encoded** array of Slack Block Kit blocks — a
    `rich_text` block is what the real composer sends for plain text).
  - `file_ids` (string, JSON-encoded array of file ID strings, e.g.
    `["F0XXXXXXX"]`) — optional, attach previously-uploaded files
    (`files.completeUploadExternal`).
  - `destinations` (string, JSON-encoded array of `{"channel_id": "..."}`
    objects). **Must be a channel/DM id (`C...`/`D...`/`G...`), not a user id**
    — passing a `U...` id gives `invalid_channel`. To DM someone, resolve their
    user id to a DM channel id first with `conversations.open`.
  - `date_scheduled` (string/int, unix timestamp — when the draft should send).
  - `client_msg_id` (string, a fresh UUID — client-generated idempotency/id key).
  - `is_from_composer` (**must be the literal `true`**). If omitted/false:
    `invalid_arguments`. If `false` and `file_ids` is also set:
    `scheduled_draft_cannot_be_attached`. The client always sends `true`; there
    doesn't appear to be a supported way to create a draft with
    `is_from_composer:false` that also carries file attachments.
- **Response:** `{"ok": true, "draft": {"id": "...", "date_scheduled": ...,
  "file_ids": [...], "destinations": [...], "last_updated_ts": "...", ...}}`.
- **Gotchas:**
  - `file_ids` can be attached to more than one draft at once (files aren't
    consumed/exclusive to a single draft).
  - `date_scheduled` in the past or too soon may be accepted by `create` but
    rejected at send time by Slack's scheduler — not tested (would require
    waiting for a real send).
- **Provenance:** prior hands-on session work with this account (see `sneply.py`
  in the sibling project), re-confirmed live this session.

```python
import json, time, uuid, requests
from urllib.parse import quote

headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {xoxc}",              # team OR enterprise xoxc both work here
    "Cookie": f"d={quote(xoxd, safe='')}",
}
blocks = [{"type": "rich_text", "elements": [
    {"type": "rich_text_section", "elements": [{"type": "text", "text": "hello, scheduled"}]}
]}]
data = {
    "blocks": json.dumps(blocks),
    "destinations": json.dumps([{"channel_id": "D0XXXXXXX"}]),  # self-DM or another channel/DM id
    "date_scheduled": str(int(time.time()) + 40 * 24 * 3600),   # >=30 days out for sandbox testing
    "client_msg_id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
    "is_from_composer": "true",
}
r = requests.post("https://slack.com/api/drafts.create", headers=headers, data=data)
```

## `drafts.list`

- **Status:** undocumented. **Live-verified.**
- **Token:** **enterprise xoxc/xoxd only** — team xoxc gives `team_is_restricted`.
- **Params:** none required for a basic listing (may support pagination
  cursors like other `*.list` methods — not explored further).
- **Response:** array of draft objects (same shape as the `draft` object
  returned by `drafts.create`).
- **Gotcha:** this returns the user's **real** drafts — read metadata only when
  actually needed, never dump/persist it, and never modify anything it shows
  that you didn't create yourself.

## `drafts.delete`

- **Status:** undocumented. **Live-verified** (sandbox cleanup only).
- **Token:** enterprise xoxc/xoxd only.
- **Params:**
  - `draft_id` (string).
  - `client_last_updated_ts` — **must be a current timestamp** (e.g.
    `f"{time.time():.6f}"` at call time), **not** the draft's own
    `last_updated_ts` from the `create`/`list` response. Passing the draft's own
    stored timestamp gives `draft_has_conflict` (Slack appears to use this as an
    optimistic-concurrency check: "the timestamp you're deleting as-of must be
    now, not whenever you last read the draft").
- **Response:** `{"ok": true}`.

## `drafts.update`

- **Status:** undocumented. **Not live-tested** (editing an existing draft is a
  pure mutation with no read-only subset — out of scope per safety rules beyond
  confirming it exists).
- **Token:** presumed enterprise xoxc/xoxd only, consistent with `list`/`delete`
  (not independently confirmed).
- **Params (inferred, not confirmed):** likely `draft_id` +
  `client_last_updated_ts` (same conflict-check pattern as `delete`) + whichever
  of `blocks`/`file_ids`/`destinations`/`date_scheduled` are being changed.
- **Provenance:** existence confirmed via oracle only this session; field-shape
  guess is by analogy to `create`/`delete`, not observed.

# The Edge API (`edgeapi.slack.com`) — a separate, out-of-scope-for-our-oracle system

**Live-tested (2026-11-02), read-only, one workspace (Hack Club, Enterprise Grid `E09V5…`), session credentials (`xoxc` + `xoxd`) of a single test account.** 17 paths exist; the rest of the write-up below is source-derived. See "Live test results" at the end.

Everything else in `methods/` goes through the standard dispatcher:
`POST https://slack.com/api/<method>` (or the workspace-hosted equivalent),
form-encoded, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The Slack web client *also* talks
to a structurally different system, the **Edge API**, at:

```
POST https://edgeapi.slack.com/cache/<enterprise_id>/<resource>/<action>
```

This is not `/api/<namespace>.<method>` — it's a REST-ish path per
resource/action, keyed by the Enterprise Grid **org id** (`E...`) in the URL
itself, and (per source material) supports JSON body in addition to
form-encoding. Our existence oracle (garbage token -> compare `unknown_method`
vs. an auth error) was built and validated only against the `/api/<method>`
dispatcher; it was never adapted or tested against this path scheme, so **none
of the endpoints below have been confirmed to exist by us** — they're recorded
purely from the reverse-engineering gist (sshh12) that documented them from
live Enterprise Grid network traffic.

## Endpoints reported (all under `/cache/<enterprise_id>/...`)

| Path | Inferred purpose |
|---|---|
| `users/info` | Single user lookup (Edge-cached variant of `users.info`). |
| `users/list` | Bulk user listing (Edge-cached variant of `users.list`). |
| `users/counts` | User-related counts. |
| `users/search` | User search. |
| `channels/info` | Single channel lookup. |
| `channels/membership` | Channel membership data. |
| `channels/search` | Channel search. |
| `permissions/info` | Permission info for some resource. |
| `huddles/info` | Huddle (Slack's voice/video call feature) info. |
| `emojis/info` | Custom emoji info. |

## Why these exist as a separate system (per source material)

The Edge API appears to be Slack's caching/fan-out layer for Enterprise Grid —
built so the client can query "give me info on user X" without re-fetching
across every team in a large org each time, keyed by a shared cache under the
enterprise id rather than per-team. `korotovsky/slack-mcp-server`'s docs
describe "intelligent API routing based on authentication type" where the
client prefers Edge API endpoints when session tokens are available (they're
faster/richer for Enterprise Grid) and falls back to the standard `/api/`
methods otherwise.

## What would be needed to properly document this

1. Adapt the existence-oracle technique (or find an equivalent) for this host —
   unclear whether a garbage token on `edgeapi.slack.com` distinguishes
   real/fake resource paths the same way, since the URL structure itself
   (not just a `method` form field) determines dispatch. Untested.
2. Confirm the actual enterprise id (`E...`) format requirement and whether a
   wrong-but-well-formed id changes the error signature in a way that leaks
   path validity.
3. Only then consider narrow read-only live tests, under the same safety rules
   as everywhere else in this project.

This is flagged in `README.md`'s honest-coverage section as a known gap, not
silently omitted.

## Live test results

**Method.** Each path was POSTed with `Authorization: Bearer <xoxc>`,
`Cookie: d=<xoxd>`, JSON body. Nonexistent paths return HTTP 404 with body
`Not Found`, so any other status means the path exists. The sweep covered 49
resource names × 21 read-style actions (`info`, `list`, `search`, `counts`,
`membership`, `get`, `fetch`, `lookup`, `status`, `members`, `metadata`,
`history`, `read`, `permissions`, `all`, `batch`, `bulk`, `details`,
`summary`, `state`, `recent`). Write-style actions (`create`, `set`, `update`,
`delete`, `send`, `join`, …) were not sent. The sweep covers only the names
guessed here, so "every endpoint" means every one that could be found, not a
complete inventory.

**Result: 17 existing paths, all returning `ok: true` with a working body.** Retested on 2026-11-03 with the enterprise-level token (`teams[0]`): all 17 still return `ok: true`. See [`read-sweep-2026-11-03.md`](read-sweep-2026-11-03.md).

| Path | Working body (keys) | Response keys | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `users/info` | `{"ids":[user_id]}` | `results` | `user`/`user_ids` → `invalid_request` |
| `users/list` | `{"channels":[id],"present_first":true,"filter":"everyone AND NOT bots AND NOT apps","count":N}` | `results`, `next_marker` | Returned 20 channel members, no bots/apps/deleted. No presence field, so `present_first` order not verified. |
| `users/counts` | `{}`-style (ok with `channels`) | `counts` | |
| `users/search` | `{"query":str,"count":N}` | `results` | |
| `channels/info` | `{"ids":[channel_id]}` | `results` | `channel`/`channel_ids` → `invalid_request` |
| `channels/list` | `{"count":N}` | `results`, `next_marker` | |
| `channels/search` | `{"query":str,"count":N}` | `results` | |
| `channels/membership` | `{"channel":id,"user":id}` | `channel` | Single pair only; `channels:[…]` → `invalid_request` |
| `permissions/info` | `{}` | `allowed`, `allowed_per_team` | |
| `huddles/info` | `{"channel_ids":[id]}` | `huddles` | `channel`/`channels` → `invalid_request` |
| `huddles/list` | `{"channel_ids":[id]}` | `huddles` | |
| `emojis/info` | `{"ids":[name]}` | `results`, `failed_ids` | Name-based `names`/`emoji` → `invalid_request`. `ids` with `white_check_mark` returned no results (`failed_ids`), so the id form is not confirmed to resolve standard emoji names. |
| `emojis/list` | `{"count":N}` | `results`, `next_marker` | |
| `emojis/search` | `{"query":str,"count":N}` | `results` | |
| `usergroups/info` | `{"ids":[id]}` | `results`, `failed_ids` | Probed with a fake id `S01`, so only the shape is confirmed. |
| `usergroups/search` | `{"query":str,"count":N}` | `results` | |
| `apps/info` | `{"ids":[id]}` | `results`, `failed_ids` | Probed with a fake id `A01`, so only the shape is confirmed. |

Newly found and not in the original write-up: `channels/list`, `emojis/list`,
`emojis/search`, `huddles/list`, `usergroups/info`, `usergroups/search`,
`apps/info`.

**Not found** (404) for the other combinations tried, for example
`nosuchresource/info`, `users/nosuchaction`, `zzz/zzz`, and any `*/create|set|…`
(not sent).

### Reported client behaviour (face stack in the channel header)

A description of Slack's web client (`BaseAvatarStack`) was checked against the
API data above.

- **Confirmed**: the Edge `users/list` call with the reported body returns
  channel members with bots and apps filtered out.
- **Partly confirmed**: the top-3 faces are the most recent distinct non-bot
  posters who are still members (checked against `conversations.history` and
  `conversations.members` on 15 channels). Some channels had no matching
  recent poster among their first 1,000 members, which fits a fallback to the
  Edge list. The fallback was not triggered in testing.
- **Not verified**: `present_first` ordering (no presence field returned), the
  lookback depth of recent messages, and the "5 faces / View all 5 members"
  label, which comes from a different selector.
- **Caveat**: `conversations.members` returns at most 1,000 IDs per page and was
  not paginated, so channels with more members are truncated in those
  comparisons.

### Safety notes

- The `users/list` probe used a channel with 387 members and `count: 20`.
- All calls were read-style. Nothing was posted, joined, or changed.
- The token pair belongs to an automation account (`auto-accountsjohnfloc`).
  Results were not written anywhere except this document.

# `files.*` — files

Documented upload/delete flow (improved with observed gotchas) plus two
undocumented methods (`files.edit`, `files.share`).

## Upload-without-a-channel flow (documented methods, working example)

1. `files.getUploadURLExternal` — params `filename`, `length` (byte count).
   Returns `{"ok": true, "file_id": "F...", "upload_url": "https://..."}`.
2. `POST` the raw file bytes directly to `upload_url` (not `slack.com/api` — a
   separate, short-lived signed upload endpoint). No Slack auth header needed
   for this step; the URL itself is the credential.
3. `files.completeUploadExternal` — params `files` (JSON array of
   `{"id": "F...", "title": "..."}`), and optionally `channel_id` if you want to
   post it immediately. Without a channel, this just finalizes the file object
   so it can be referenced by `file_ids` elsewhere (e.g. `drafts.create`).
- **Gotcha:** the same `file_id` can be attached to **multiple** drafts — files
  aren't consumed/exclusive.

## Hosting an image for a bot's `icon_url` (live-tested 2026-10-23, bot `xoxb`)

Goal: get a Slack-hosted image that `chat.postMessage`'s `icon_url` (or an
image block) can load, because Slack fetches those with no auth.

- **Uploading works with a bot token** (`files:write`). `files.getUploadURLExternal`
  returned `ok:true`; a `multipart/form-data` `POST` (field `file`) to
  `upload_url` returned HTTP 200; `files.completeUploadExternal` with just
  `files: [{id, title}]` returned `ok:true`. The file is then private to the
  uploader: `files.info` shows `channels: []`, `groups: []`, `ims: []`,
  `is_public: false`, `public_url_shared: false`.
- **`permalink_public` is present but dead until a public link exists.**
  `files.info` on that unshared file already returns a
  `https://slack-files.com/T…-F…-<secret>` value in `permalink_public`, but it
  returns HTTP 404 until a public link is actually created.
- **`files.sharedPublicURL` could not create the link from either token we
  have.** The bot `xoxb` got `not_allowed_token_type`. The workspace's
  configured user token got `missing_scope` (we did not capture the
  `needed`/`provided` fields, so which scope is missing is unconfirmed).
- **The web/desktop client's "Copy public link" does work** (tried by hand;
  the workspace allows public file links). It yields
  `https://slack-files.com/T…-F…-<10 hex chars>`. That URL serves an **HTML
  viewer page** (200, `text/html`), not the image. Its `og:image` meta tag
  points at the real bytes:
  `https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T…-F…/<name>?pub_secret=<the same 10 hex chars>`.
  That URL returns the raw PNG (200, `image/png`) with no auth, so it is the
  one to use as `icon_url`.
- **Without `pub_secret`, a `files-pri` URL is not fetchable.** The bare
  `https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T…-F…/<name>` answers `302` to the
  workspace login page (`https://<workspace>.slack.com/?redir=…`).
- **A bot cannot see a file a user uploaded and never shared with it:**
  `files.info` on such a file returned `file_not_found`.
- **Caveats:** the public link only lasts while the workspace allows public
  links and nobody revokes it, and an uploaded file counts as workspace
  storage. We ended up hosting the image on our own CDN instead.
- **Slack's own RSS app icon** is served from
  `https://a.slack-edge.com/80588/img/services/rss_<size>.png`: sizes 72, 96,
  128, 192, 512 and 1024 all returned 200; 256 returned 403 (live `curl`,
  2026-10-23). The `80588` segment is a build id and may change.

## `files.delete` (documented)

- Standard cleanup call, `file` param = file id. Used here for sandbox cleanup
  after test uploads. `{"ok": true}` on success.

## `files.edit`

- **Status:** UNDOCUMENTED.
- **Purpose (inferred):** edit an already-uploaded file's content and/or title
  in place, distinct from re-uploading. Likely powers the web client's "Edit
  this file" action on Slack Canvases/snippets.
- **Existence:** confirmed via oracle.
- **Live-tested:** no — mutating.
- **Provenance:** `slack-ruby/slack-api-ref`,
  `methods/_undocumented/files/files.edit.json`; also listed independently in
  `ErikKalkoken/slackApiDoc`.
- **Params (cross-referenced from `ErikKalkoken/slackApiDoc`, not independently
  verified here):** `token` (required), `file` (required, file ID), `title`
  (required, new title), `filetype` (optional, new filetype). Response is a
  full updated file object.

## `files.share`

- **Status:** UNDOCUMENTED.
- **Purpose (inferred):** share an already-uploaded (unshared) file into one or
  more channels — the step that used to be separate from upload in Slack's
  older (pre-`getUploadURLExternal`) file API, and still appears to exist as an
  internal call.
- **Existence:** confirmed via oracle.
- **Live-tested:** no — mutating (posts into a channel).
- **Provenance:** `slack-ruby/slack-api-ref`,
  `methods/_undocumented/files/files.share.json`; also in
  `ErikKalkoken/slackApiDoc`.
- **Params (cross-referenced from `ErikKalkoken/slackApiDoc`, not independently
  verified here):** `token` (required, legacy token per their notes), `file`
  (required, file ID), `channel` (required — works with both public channel
  IDs and private-channel/group IDs).

<!-- Source: Slack file F0CBSH98EP8 (GATEWAY_EVENTS.md, created 2026-10-24), fetched 2026-11-06. -->

# Slack web client — realtime ("gateway") events

Mined from the de-bundled `app.slack.com/client` JS in `slack-debundle/modules/`.
Slack has no component literally called "gateway"; the equivalent is the
**realtime websocket to the message server (MS)**, called **RTM** in the code.
Every inbound frame is JSON `{ type, subtype?, event_ts?, ...payload }`.

**Coverage:** 341 distinct inbound event types registered through the router
(`modern_vendor/4221__30LT.js`), plus `message` (documented first, with its subtypes),
plus the transport-level frames and the outbound frames below.

**Caveat on shapes:** payloads are reconstructed from how the client *reads* them
(no server schema exists in the bundle). Fields are those the client touches;
objects passed whole into a store are marked pass-through. The per-event sections
were produced by reading the handler and its direct helpers; most reducers/thunks
downstream were *not* followed, so "unverified"/"inferred" marks are meaningful.
Handler line numbers in the per-event sections are registration lines in the
named file unless stated.

## 1. Transport layer

### Socket (`modern_vendor/1609__1JlF.js`, class `SlackSocket`)
| Frame | Dir | Shape / behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| reply | in | any frame with `reply_to: number` resolves the pending send with that `id`; `ok === true` is treated as the reject branch in `handleReply` (code quirk) |
| `hello` | in | `{type:"hello", flannel?, region, self?, start?}`. Fires `onConnectCallback({useFlannel: flannel, region})`; if `start` present it resolves the start-data promise as `{self, region, ...start}`, otherwise start data is cancelled |
| `error` | in | `{type:"error", error:{...}}` → `onErrorMessageCallback(error)` → `handleErrorMessage`. Start-error codes handled: `user_removed_from_team`, `account_inactive`, `team_disabled`, `invalid_auth`, `two_factor_setup_required`, `force_reload`, `clear_cache`, `org_login_required`, `team_added_to_org`, `ratelimited`, `accesslimited`, `user_in_no_workspaces`; `started_with_org_token` is logged; anything else throws "Unknown start error" |
| everything else | in | passed to the message delegate → per-workspace queue → router |
| `ping` | out | `{type:"ping", id}` every 10 s; socket closed (code 4998) if no reply for 90 s |
| `tickle` | out | `{type:"tickle", reason, id}` ("ping the message server"), sent at most every ~19 s, fire-and-forget (no reply awaited) |

Every outbound frame gets an auto-increment `id` (starts at 16385); frames over 32768 bytes are rejected.
Close codes used locally: 4999 (default manual close), 4998 (pong timeout).

### Router / queue (`4221__30LT.js`, `4190__3avk.js`)
- Registrars: `addRtmHandler(type, fn(msg, dispatch, getState))` (per message), `addBatchRtmHandler(type, fn(msgs, dispatch, getState))`, `addSharedRtmHandler(type, fn(msgs, teamOrEnterpriseId))`. Duplicate registration throws.
- Queue per workspace/enterprise. Consecutive messages with the same `type`+`subtype` are batched (adaptive batch size 1–100). Event types in the "interleavable" set can be hopped over while batching: `accounts_changed, benchmark, bot_changed, channel_changed, channel_marked, client_logs_request, commands_changed, desktop_notification, draft_create, email_domain_changed, file_change, file_created, file_public, file_shared, file_unshared, group_marked, im_marked, manual_presence_change, mpim_marked, team_rename, user_change, user_invalidated, user_typing`.
- Frames with `_from_evt_log` were replayed from `eventlog.history` after a reconnect/resync; frames with `event_ts` advance the last-seen timestamp (not for replays).
- Before dispatch, `message` frames are preprocessed (30 s cap): ensures the channel model exists (`channel` string id), fetches member counts when text has mention patterns, and opens the conversation if needed.
- Unregistered types are silently dropped. Degraded mode can call handlers directly (`handleMessageImmediatelyWithoutPreprocessing`).

### Outbound frames (client → MS)
| `type` | Shape | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `presence_sub` | `{ids: string[]}` | subscribe to presence for these user ids (refcounted per member; re-sent on change, throttled 100 ms) |
| `subscription_update` | `{subtype, ids: string[]}`; subtypes `user_change_subscribe_request`, `user_change_unsubscribe_request`, `dnd_invalidated_subscribe_request`, `dnd_invalidated_unsubscribe_request` | subscribe to `user_change` / `dnd_invalidated` pushes for specific users (max ids per call enforced client side) |
| `flannel` | `{subtype: <method>, ...args}` | request to the Flannel cache service over the socket (args must not contain `type`/`subtype`); also available over HTTP |
| `temp_channel_sub` / `temp_channel_unsub` | `{channel_id}` | temporary subscription to a channel/file/canvas topic (used for awareness & file/canvas live updates) |
| `awareness` | `{channel, user, subtype: "query"\|"broadcast"\|"close", awareness_state?}` | collaborative presence on a topic; mirrored by the inbound `awareness` event |
| `document_change` | `{user, channel, payload: base64 string}` | canvas/doc collaborative edit update (binary op encoded with `btoa`); mirrored by inbound `document_change` / `document_update` |

## 2. `message` and its subtypes

- **Registrar:** shared (`addSharedRtmHandler`) → `messageReceived(msgs, dispatch, getState)`; also consumed in `modern_vendor` preprocessing.
- **Batching key is `type`+`subtype`**, so a batch is homogeneous; the first element's `subtype` picks the branch.
- **Base payload:** `{type:"message", subtype?, channel: string, ts: string, user?: string, text?: string, thread_ts?: string, client_msg_id?: string, files?: (string|{id})[], attachments?: any[], event_ts?: string, bot_id?, ai_context?: {uses_remaining?: number, result_status?: "streaming"|"complete", follow_up_suggestion?: string}, streaming_state?: string, ...}` (a full message object; unspecified fields are passed through to the message store).
- **Default path for all subtypes** (`messageReceivedDefault` + loop): reconciles with pending local sends via `client_msg_id` (undo-send deletion, placeholder file-id check), upserts message, upserts thread/agent-thread data when the channel is an agent conversation, tracks huddle-notes autostart, triggers desktop notification, activity-feed entries (`at_user`, `dm`, `internal_channel_invite`), "new message" toast, thread unread marks, unfurl/AI streaming bookkeeping.

Subtypes the client switches on (non-exhaustive: other subtypes are rendered but get only the default path):

| subtype | Extra payload read | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `message_changed` | `channel`, `message` (new full message, needs `ts`), `previous_message?`, `event_ts`, `_from_evt_log` | upserts edited message; drops stale local state if message became hidden/unmentioned; AI-streaming transitions (`ai_context.result_status`, `follow_up_suggestion`), unfurl diffing, DLP rescans, Slackbot handoff navigation (`handoff_thread_ts=…`, `handoff_channel=…` in text) |
| `message_deleted` | `deleted_ts`, `channel`, `previous_message?`, `event_ts`, `_from_evt_log` | removes message + thread data, updates last-message state |
| `message_replied` | `channel`, `message` (parent with `ts`, `latest_reply?`, `replies?: {ts}[]`), `event_ts` | upserts the parent thread message; ignores event if older than local `latest_reply` |
| `message_locked` | `channel`, `thread_ts`, `is_locked: boolean`, `locked_by_team_id?` | marks thread locked/unlocked |
| `thread_broadcast` | message | default path only |
| `channel_history_changed` / `group_…` / `im_…` / `mpim_…` | – | ignored here (handled by the same-named top-level events) |
| `channel_purpose` / `group_purpose` | `channel`, `user`, `ts`, `purpose` | updates channel purpose `{creator, last_set, value}` |
| `channel_topic` / `group_topic` | `channel`, `user`, `ts`, `topic` | updates channel topic |
| `document_mention` | `user`, `channel`, `ts`, `document_mention:{file_id, mentioning_user_ids[], section_id}` | activity-feed `at_user` entry + canvas mention state |
| `channel_canvas_updated` | `channel`, `ts`, `canvas_update_user_ids: string[]` | marks channel canvas updated for current user |
| `tabbed_canvas_updated` | same | marks canvas tab updated |
| `channel_tab_added` | `channel`, `ts`, `tab_added_user_id` | marks channel dirty when added by self |
| `folder_item_added` | `channel`, `ts`, `item_added_user_id` | same |
| `channel_join` | `channel`, `ts`, `user`, `inviter?`, `thread_ts?` | internal_channel_invite feed entry |
| `prejoin_dm_welcome_party_notification` | `channel`, `ts` | `dm` feed entry |
| `automatic_ai_huddle_notes_enabled` / `_disabled` | `user`, `channel` | records huddle-notes autostart change |
| other subtypes the client special-cases elsewhere | – | `bot_message`, `pinned_item`, `unpinned_item`, `sh_room_created`, `sh_room_shared`, `huddle_thread`, `huddle_message`, `scheduled_huddle_message`, `scheduled_huddle_canceled`, `huddle_notes_started`, `tombstone`, `file_comment`, `file_share`, `reply_broadcast`, `assistant_app_thread`, `assistant_app_initial_thread`, `slackbot_response`, `app_conversation_join`, `group_join`, `joiner_notification_for_inviter`, `mpdm_move`, `list_record_comment`, `list_edit`, `document_comment_root`, `surface_card_comment`, `canvas_sharing_message`, `slack_assistant_progress`, `agent_view_added`, `ms_oauth_completed`, `retention`, `dashboard`, `poll`, `digest`, `bookmark_created`, `bookmark_removed`, `copy_link`, `click_link_in_canvas` (rendering/analytics logic keyed on subtype) |

# 3. Per-event reference (all 340 other registered events)

### `agentforce_agent_status_updated`
- **Registrar:** single
- **Handler:** `(anonymous arrow)` (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:35541)
- **Purpose:** An Agentforce agent app changed availability/status or description. Client dispatches two status-updating actions (Tm.vg, Tp.Fk) and, if a description is present, an assistant-description update (Tp.Ms).
- **Payload:**
  ```ts
  {
    type: "agentforce_agent_status_updated";
    app_id?: string;                 // agent app id; required for any action
    status?: string;                 // agent status (required with app_id for status actions)
    is_available?: boolean;          // passed through as isAvailable (inferred)
    assistant_description?: string;  // dispatches description update if present
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** Status actions need app_id and status both truthy; description action needs app_id and assistant_description.

  ```ts
  }
  ```

### `app_actions_updated`

### `dialog_opened`
- **Registrar:** single
- **Handler:** `(anonymous arrow)` (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:36812)
- **Purpose:** Server asks the client to open a legacy app dialog (after a slash command / interactive component trigger). Client verifies the `client_token` belongs to a pending local trigger and is fresh, then opens a modal dialog element.
- **Payload:**
  ```ts
  {
    type: "dialog_opened";
    app_id: string;
    client_token: string;         // matched against locally-registered pending triggers (Ty.A.check); embeds a timestamp (getTimeDelta)
    dialog_id: string;
    dialog_title: string;
    dialog_submit_label: string;
    timeout_range: number;        // max allowed age of the token; ignored if delta >= timeout_range
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** Ignored if token not found in local state. Tracks APP_DIALOG_OPEN_ATTEMPTED analytics. Calls token's onDialogOpen callback.

### `view_opened`
- **Registrar:** single
- **Handler:** `viewOpened` (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:37763)
- **Purpose:** A Block Kit view was opened/pushed by an app. For modals it validates the client token and freshness, shows the app-view modal (or stacks it); for home views it records the home view for the channel. The view is stored via the normalized-view reducer.

  ```ts
    client_token?: string;     // required for modal types (else ignored)
    timeout_range?: number;
    title?: object;           // modal title (passed to modal opener)
    submit?: object;          // submit button (passed through)
    close?: object;           // close button (passed through)
    app_id?: string;
    channel_id?: string;      // used for "home" views
    trace_id?: string;
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** For modals, ignored unless token matches local trigger (except special "search_and_ai_feedback:submit" callback id); also ignored when a gating predicate (Iz.A) is on. Tracks APPVIEW_RECEIVED/OPENED/STACKED.

### `list_record_updated`
- **Registrar:** single
- **Handler:** inline arrow (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:40129)
- **Purpose:** A list record changed. If `deleted`, removes it; otherwise normalizes and upserts the record, and if it is assigned to the current user ("my item") also dispatches a my-item action.
- **Payload:**
  ```ts
  {
    type: "list_record_updated";
    list_id: string;
    id: string;            // record id (used for delete)
    deleted?: boolean;
    record?: {
      fields?: unknown[];  // inspected to decide if it concerns current user
      // ...full record object, normalized by hR.jG (fields unverified)
    };
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** Gated on Lists enabled. Ignored if `record` missing and not deleted.

### `list_cells_updated`
- **Registrar:** single
- **Handler:** inline arrow (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:40171)
- **Purpose:** Cell values (and optionally a column definition) changed in a list. Client replaces the matching schema column in the list's metadata and applies cell updates to the cached list records.
- **Payload:**
  ```ts
  {
    type: "list_cells_updated";
    list_id: string;
    column?: { key: string; /* ...full column schema object, replaces entry in list_metadata.schema */ };
    cells: unknown; // cell update objects, passed to N9.VR (shape unverified)
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** Does nothing if the list is not in the local store. Schema replacement skipped when matching index is 0 or -1 (quirk of `s &&`).

### `user_change`
- **Registrar:** single
- **Handler:** `userChange` (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:40534)
- **Purpose:** A user profile changed. For other users, their member record is marked stale/refetched. For the current user, the member is applied eagerly (when experiment `eager_apply_user_change` is on) or refetched, team permissions are marked stale, and role flags (primary owner/owner/admin) are updated in the store.
- **Payload:**
  ```ts
  {
    type: "user_change";
    user: {
      id: string;
      team_id?: string;
      enterprise_id?: string;          // if set, treated as org-scoped member
      is_primary_owner?: boolean;
      is_owner?: boolean;
      is_admin?: boolean;
      enterprise_user?: {              // org-level roles
        is_primary_owner?: boolean;
        is_owner?: boolean;
        is_admin?: boolean;
      };
      // ...full user/member object (passed to members reducer when eager apply is on)
    };
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** Logs a warning if event scope (org vs workspace) differs from stored member. Ignored if `user` missing.

### `open_agent_conversation`
- **Registrar:** single
- **Handler:** `handleOpenAgentConversation` (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:44136)
- **Purpose:** A workflow "send to agent" step asks this client to open an agent conversation. For a 3p agent it posts `prompt_blocks` as a DM to the agent and navigates to the thread; otherwise it opens the Slackbot DM in split view and sends the prompt as a Slackbot AI message. Afterwards it calls `functions.workflows.executions.confirmDelivery` with delivered true/false.
- **Payload:**
  ```ts
  {
    type: "open_agent_conversation";
    client_token?: string;          // if set, must be in the client's pending-token queue, else discarded
    timeout_ms?: number;            // if token age >= this, treated as expired (delivered=false)
    agent_user_id?: string;         // if set: third-party agent flow (DM with that agent); else Slackbot flow
    prompt_blocks: object[];        // Block Kit blocks; posted as message blocks (3p) or converted to delta (Slackbot)
    workflow_id?: string;           // sent in client_context for Slackbot flow
    function_execution_id?: string; // if set, confirmDelivery is called and thread is linked to the execution
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** Response from confirmDelivery (`workflow_name`, `is_continuable`) is used to register a continuable thread. Without function_execution_id no confirmation is made.

### `ai_summary_completed`
- **Registrar:** single
- **Handler:** `handleAiSummaryCompletion` (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:45553)
- **Purpose:** Final result of a Slack AI summary; client branches on `summary.metadata.type` (crm_email_draft, ai_explain, search, canvas, today_topic, composer, else channel/thread/recap summary) and stores content/status/errors.
- **Payload:**
  ```ts
  {
    type: "ai_summary_completed";
    event_ts?: string; // today_topic: floor(parseFloat) -> dateUpdated
    summary: {
      id: string;
      ai_context_result_status: "complete" | "no_answer" | "failed" | "pending" | string;
      error?: string;                // e.g. "channel_excluded"
      suggested_prompts?: string[];  // search (inferred)
      result?: {
        text?: string;
        blocks?: object[];
        description_blocks?: object[];                          // channel/thread
        topics?: { id: string; topic?: string; blocks?: object[] }[];
      };
      file_sources?: object[];       // canvas
      message_sources?: object[];    // canvas
      metadata?: {
        type?: "crm_email_draft" | "ai_explain" | "search" | "canvas" | "today_topic" | "composer" | string; // other => channel/thread summary
        channel_id?: string;
        thread?: { start_ts: string; end_ts?: string };
        channel?: { thread_count?: number; start_ts?: string; end_ts?: string };
        is_keywords?: boolean;
        query?: string;               // search/canvas prompt
        relevant_entities?: object;
        has_source_different_from_user_lang?: boolean;
        message_count?: number;
        file_count?: number;
        info_message?: string;
        canvas?: { id: string };      // canvas file id; id "SLACKBOT_CANVAS_AUTO_OPEN" special-cases auto-opening the canvas
        most_active_users?: unknown;
        total_involved_users?: unknown;
        total_message_count?: number;
        channels?: object[];
      };
    };
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** Handler source was truncated in the dossier near the end of the channel/thread branch, so remaining fields there are unverified. For ai_explain, ignored unless the summary id is known locally.

### `room_update`
- **Registrar:** single
- **Handler:** `huddleRoomUpdatedHandler` (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:46517)
- **Purpose:** Updates on a huddle "knock" (request to join) room. Handles request accepted (joins with media credentials), expired (resets knock UI), and the list of users currently waiting to be let in.
- **Payload:**
  ```ts
  {
    type: "room_update";
    channel_id: string;
    knock_status?: "accepted" | "expired" | string; // only these two values are acted upon
    free_willy?: object;       // media server credentials, passed through as mediaServerCredentials (opaque)
    knocking_users?: string[]; // user ids waiting to join; used for expiry check (includes own id) and waiting list
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** Only acted on if `tI.pt(state)` (huddle-enabled). "accepted" requires `free_willy`; shows toast "Your request to join the huddle is approved". "expired" only if own user id is in `knocking_users`; shows "huddle request has expired" toast. The waiting list is stored only if the user is a huddle host-like (`oH.$V`) and not (`Le.U`). Note `knocking_users.includes` is called unguarded on "expired".

### `sh_room_join`

- **Purpose:** A participant joined a Slack call/huddle room. Client normalizes `room` and upserts it in call state; for huddles it also drives recording-notice, transcript and UI state. Shares handler with `sh_room_leave` and `sh_room_update`.

  ```ts
  {

      participants?: any[];        // length is logged
      knocks?: any;                // passed via normalizer
      last_invite_status_by_user?: Record<string, any>; // passed via normalizer
      // full room object passed to normalizer Lr.Q; other fields not enumerated
    };
    huddle?: {
      channel_id: string;          // present => huddle path (when huddles on)
    };
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** If `huddle` is present and huddles/other flag are on, runs `updateHuddleRtmHandler`; otherwise generic call path. When the own user joins and a local huddle state exists, waits 10s and aborts if the stored call changed. Own join may dismiss calendar JIT and trigger recording-on sound/notice.

### `user_typing`
- **Registrar:** shared
- **Handler:** `ArrowFunctionExpression` (anonymous, batch-of-msgs + teamOrEnterpriseId) (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:46557)

  ```ts
  }
  ```

- **Notes:** Only in gantry (org-wide) context else throws; skipped when document hidden, when the `show_typing` pref is off, when the channel is unknown, or the user isn't a valid target (`aZ.TO` filter, e.g. self/muted). Dispatches `Mt.W({channelId, threadTs, memberIds})`.

### `channel_updated`
- **Registrar:** single
- **Handler:** `channelUpdated` (modules/eager/application/0620__HVn0.js:47080)
- **Purpose:** Partial update to one or more channels. Client merges `updates` into the cached channel (upsert) plus side effects: archive/unarchive, permissions (read-only/thread-only), space prefs, topic, canvas/meeting-notes properties, membership stale-marking, removal if converted to private without membership.
- **Payload:**
  ```ts
  {
    type: "channel_updated";
    channel?: string;     // single channel id
    channels?: string[];  // or list of channel ids (takes priority)
    updates: {            // partial channel fields, merged into the channel (also has any other channel field)
      is_archived?: boolean;          // true => archive path, false => unarchive path
      user?: string;                  // (from top-level spread on archive) see Notes
      permissions?: { post?: any; thread?: any }; // converted to is_read_only / is_thread_only
      space?: { space_icon?: string; space_file_id?: string; space_is_primary?: boolean }; // stored as channel prefs
      is_migrating?: boolean;         // true->false triggers reload
      is_mpim?: boolean;              // false => mpim converted to private channel
      unlinked?: any;                 // presence => connected-teams refresh
      connected_team_ids?: string[];  // presence => connected-teams refresh
      membership?: any;               // presence => mark channel stale and refetch
      topic?: { value: string; creator: string; last_set: number|string };
      properties?: {
        has_slack_connect_invite_created?: boolean;
        canvas?: { file_id: string };
        meeting_notes?: { file_id: string }; // "" clears meeting notes view
        record_channel?: { minimum_access_level?: any };
      };
      [other: string]: any;           // any other channel field merged as-is
    };
  }
  ```
- **Notes:** Ignored for unknown channels or if `updates` is missing. For `is_archived` it calls the archive/unarchive logic with `{channel, ...updates}` (so archive moved/frozen data may be taken from updates; unarchive reads `user` and compares to own id with pref `public_channel_retain_membership_on_archive`). Channel converted to private where user is not a member is removed. The `user` field in `updates` for unarchive is inferred from the helper reading `e.user` on the merged object (unverified).
